# GA4 Name Changer

> Google Analytics (GA4) Name Changer for Chrome Extension Developers is a free, open-source
> Chrome extension that replaces the 32-character Chrome Web Store extension IDs and 9-digit
> Google Analytics account numbers displayed on analytics.google.com with the extensions' real
> names. It derives those names from the user's own Google Analytics reports, so naming makes
> no network request and no analytics data is ever transmitted. The extension's only outbound
> request is the optional feedback form, sent when the user submits it.

## The problem it solves

When Google shares Chrome Web Store analytics with a developer, each extension appears in
Google Analytics 4 as an opaque 32-character property slug, which is the extension's own ID
(for example `inkkcgalfjninhfflfhkflidilkjmhof`). Every Chrome Web Store developer account is
additionally given the identical label "Chrome Web Store developer properties", distinguished
only by a 9-digit account number. These names are assigned by Google and are not editable in
the Google Analytics admin, so a developer publishing more than one extension has to keep a
mental lookup table to read their own reports. GA4 Name Changer substitutes readable names at
display time in the browser.

## How the naming works

The extension does not look anything up. A Chrome Web Store developer property's "Page title
and screen class" report lists the store listing pages that were viewed, and the Chrome Web
Store titles every listing page `<Extension Name> - <localised store name>`. Splitting each
title on the last occurrence of `" - "` therefore yields the extension's name: the split works
in every language the store is published in, and preserves extension names that themselves
contain `" - "`. Generic store pages such as "Chrome Web Store - Extensions" are discarded and
the remaining candidates are ranked by views.

An account is named after the extensions it holds, paired using Google Analytics' own account
tree. An account holding several extensions gets a combined label capped to fit the Google
Analytics breadcrumb; extensions the account holds that have not been named yet are counted
rather than guessed at, so a half-explored account reads "... + 1 more" and rewrites itself as
the rest are opened. Every derived name is a draft the user can type over, and a name the user
types always wins.

A second, optional source is `chrome.management.get()`, which reads the name of an extension
installed in the user's own Chrome profile. It is off by default, gated behind the optional
`management` permission, reads only the `name` field, never calls `getAll()`, and is handed
back to Chrome via `chrome.permissions.remove()` when switched off. It exists because Chrome
deliberately blocks extensions from requesting the Chrome Web Store, so a public extension name
cannot be fetched.

## Key facts

- Name: Google Analytics (GA4) Name Changer for Chrome Extension Developers
- Short name: GA4 Name Changer
- Category: developer tool, Chrome browser extension
- Price: free
- Version: 1.1.0
- Platform: Google Chrome 88 or later, Manifest V3
- Runs on: analytics.google.com only
- Network requests: none, except the optional feedback form when the user submits it
- Analytics data transmitted: none, ever
- Data collected: only the name, email, message and installation details a user types into the
  feedback form and submits. Never sold. Used solely to answer the report
- Licence: MIT
- Required permissions: `storage`, plus host access to `https://analytics.google.com/*`
- Optional permissions: `management`, off by default
- Dependencies: none. Plain JavaScript, no build step, no bundler, no remote code
- Publisher: PalWorks
- Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Google
